benchmark: Neuron metadata guard open-set image-classification diagnostic

protocol.split: stratified 75/25 train/test; known training pool further split 85/15 fit/calibration; random_state=2026
protocol.features: L2-normalized flattened pixels; class score is mean top-3 cosine similarities
protocol.guard_source: Metadata guard functions and thresholds from NEURONALLVERSION/Untitled36.ipynb, applied to normalized exemplar embeddings
protocol.cnn: two-convolution CPU CNN, 18 epochs, trained on the same fit split of known classes
protocol.cnn_rejection_calibration: confidence threshold chosen at the 5th percentile of max-softmax confidence on separate known-only validation images; unknown test labels were not used
protocol.limitation: This is a reproducible small-image guard-policy experiment, not the full face-recognition pipeline and not a FaceNet embedding test.

interpretation: On this one fixed split, guarded Neuron has 97.79% known-class end-to-end accuracy versus 95.86% for the same CNN in closed-set mode. Against a CNN with confidence rejection calibrated on known-only validation data, Neuron keeps 98.34% known coverage with 99.44% selective accuracy; the calibrated CNN keeps 90.61% coverage with 98.78% selective accuracy and rejects more unknown-class images (67.05% versus 59.09%). This is promising for this toy task, not proof of full-architecture superiority.
